acceptanceCriteria: The orchestration procedure (lane charter or orchestrator guidance) caps concurrently running Go-test-heavy lanes by measured host pressure (default at most 3-4 on this host); docs-only lanes may exceed it.
The cap reuses the existing host-pressure signal (V1-0694 level) or documents why it cannot.
A retained before/after measurement over at least one batch shows median load average and focused-test duration with the cap applied.
body: Evidence: owner-requested audit on 2026-10-17 of orchestrator session 03e2afac (Handoff 2026-10-14): 206 Claude Code lane subagents, 374 lane-hours over 77 h wall. Measured from subagent transcripts under ~/.claude/projects/-Users-russelllewis-projects-corvint/03e2afac-.../subagents (tool_use to tool_result timestamps) and live host reads. Toolchain: corvint-tasks 0.0.0-tcp01-unverified+build.615, Go 1.27.2, macOS 12-core/64 GB host. Lanes dispatched with the Claude Code Agent tool do not go through the corvint-tasks dispatch host-pressure throttle (V1-0694, V1-0862, V1-0891), so nothing caps them by host load. Observed: 2,462 uptime samples in lane output had load median 59.95, p90 79.84, max 245.84 on 12 cores. Memory compressor held about 18 GB; 9.0M swapouts; disk 96% full. Focused `go test -run` averaged 1.8 min over 1,962 runs, and several lanes spent hours deflaking tests that flake under load (V1-1532, V1-1495, V1-1392). Expected: lane concurrency follows host capacity. Actual: a fixed cap of 5 then 7 lanes, set by owner instruction, regardless of load. That load caused the slowdowns is an inference from the timings, not a controlled measurement.
title: Orchestrator lanes bypass the host-pressure throttle: 7 concurrent Claude Code lanes kept a 12-core host at load average 60 for 77 h
